title: 5 Best Enterprise No-Code Email Builders (2026)
summary: Compare Dyspatch, Stripo, RGE Studio (formerly Beefree), Knak and Stensul on governance, localization, AI agent support, AMP and testing. Updated November 2026.
body_markdown:
**The best enterprise no-code email builder depends on where your team gets stuck.** Dyspatch fits global, multi-brand teams that need governance, localization and AI agents that build on-brand emails. Stripo fits teams exporting to many ESPs. RGE Studio (formerly Beefree) fits smaller teams. Knak fits Marketo and Eloqua teams that also need landing pages. Stensul fits teams focused on accessibility and Adobe workflows.


*Disclosure: Dyspatch publishes this guide. We describe each tool from its own documentation and public pricing as of November 2026, and we say where a competitor is the better fit.*


## Quick guide: 5 best enterprise no-code email builders


Tool Best for Not ideal for


Dyspatch Global, multi-brand teams; AI agent email production; localizations at scale Teams that also need a landing page builder


Stripo Agencies and teams sending from many ESPs Teams with complex, multi-locale approval workflows


RGE Studio (formerly Beefree) Small teams and freelancers; product teams embedding an editor via Beefree SDK Large enterprise programs that need governance on every plan


Knak Marketo and Eloqua teams producing emails and landing pages Teams that want public pricing or a self-serve trial


Stensul Teams with strict accessibility rules and Adobe or Figma workflows Teams that want public pricing or a free plan


## How we evaluated each builder


We scored each tool on seven criteria that matter once many people, brands and locales touch the same template.


- **Brand governance:** Can you lock colors, fonts and layouts so every email stays on brand without a design review on every send?
- **Collaboration and approvals:** Are comments, role-based permissions and multi-step approvals built in?
- **Localization:** Can you manage many locales and connect to a translation management system (TMS) without duplicating work?
- **ESP and MAP integrations:** Does the tool push finished templates to platforms like Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Iterable or Marketo?
- **Rendering and testing:** Are templates responsive by default, with built-in email client previews?
- **AI and agent support:** Can AI agents such as Claude or ChatGPT build emails from your approved components, through MCP (Model Context Protocol) or a similar connection, without breaking your brand?

### 1. Dyspatch: Best for governance, localization and AI agent workflows


Dyspatch is the email design system built for AI agents. Teams and agents build marketing, lifecycle and transactional emails from approved blocks and themes, then export them to any sending platform. It's the strongest fit for global brands that need governance, 300+ locales and intuitive WYSIWYG editor to build templates


**Best for:** global, multi-brand teams; teams using AI agents to produce email; teams that want interactive email.


**Not ideal for:** teams that need a landing page builder in the same tool.


*The Dyspatch email builder.*


#### What sets it apart


- **Built for AI agents:** The Dyspatch MCP server and[Agent Operators](https://www.dyspatch.io/platform/mcp-agent-operators-in-dyspatch/) let agents like Claude build emails from your workspaces, themes, blocks and brand guidelines. Agents work inside the same guardrails as your team.
- **Governance:**[Brand guardrails](https://www.dyspatch.io/platform/email-guardrails/) lock colors, fonts and editable regions. Multi-step approvals and annotated comments keep feedback in one auditable place.
- **Localization at scale:** Support for 300+ locales, with direct integrations to Smartling, Phrase, XTM and Crowdin, plus PO/POT file support. Template locking prevents edits after approval. One Fortune 500 customer scaled to 127+ locales and sped up time to market by 250%.
- **Rendering and testing:** Dyspatch Markup Language (DML) makes every template responsive by default. Integrated Litmus previews cover email clients and devices before you send.
- **Design handoff:**[Figma Importer](https://www.dyspatch.io/platform/figma-to-html-email-export/) brings Figma email designs into Dyspatch as editable emails.
- **Integrations:** Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Iterable, SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES, Klaviyo and more, via API or direct sync.


#### Pros


- Intuitive WYSIWYG editor to build templates
- One of the deepest localization toolsets in the category
- AI agents build within your brand rules, not around them
- Built-in Litmus testing removes a separate QA tool


#### Cons


- Teams moving from raw HTML need time to learn DML
- No landing page builder; Dyspatch focuses on email and other message channels


### 2. Stripo: Best for exporting to many ESPs


Stripo is a drag-and-drop email editor that exports to 90+ ESPs and marketing platforms. It suits agencies and teams that send from several platforms and want a large template library and real-time co-editing.


**Best for:** agencies and multi-ESP teams.


**Not ideal for:** teams that need deep, multi-locale approval workflows.


*The Stripo editor. Screenshot:[Stripo Help Center](https://support.stripo.email/en/articles/6446095-what-are-the-basic-blocks-how-to-use-them) .*


#### Key features


- **90+ ESP exports:** Push templates to sending platforms, or download HTML, PDF or image files.
- **Built-in email client testing:** Stripo's[embedded testing tool](https://support.stripo.email/en/articles/3174221-how-to-test-email-templates-across-multiple-email-clients) runs on Email on Acid, so you can preview across clients and devices inside the editor.
- **Collaboration:** Real-time co-editing, comments and status tracking.
- **Enterprise controls:** The Prime plan adds custom roles and permissions, unlimited projects and unlimited exports.


#### Pros


- Broadest ESP export list in this comparison
- Transparent pricing below the enterprise tier


#### Cons


- Localization is lighter: a built-in translation service, but check whether it fits your TMS and locale approval process
- Custom roles and the highest user limits are reserved for Prime


**Pricing:** Free plan available. Paid plans start at $20/month; Prime is custom priced. On[AWS Marketplace](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-mnik4fpzpt7sg) , Prime for 50 users is listed at $15,000/year.


### 3. RGE Studio (formerly Beefree): Best for small teams and embedded editing


RGE Studio is the drag-and-drop email and landing page builder previously called Beefree. On May 14, 2026 it[moved under the Really Good Emails brand](https://beefree.io/blog/beefree-to-rge-studio) ; accounts, pricing and templates carried over. Beefree SDK, the embeddable editor for software companies, kept the Beefree name and is now a separate product.


**Best for:** small teams and freelancers; product teams that want to embed an editor (via Beefree SDK).


**Not ideal for:** large enterprise programs that need governance on every plan.


*The RGE Studio builder. Screenshot:[RGE Studio Help Center](https://support.reallygoodemails.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004546011-Settings-Rows-and-Content-How-do-they-work) .*


#### Key features


- **1,700+ templates:** A large library, plus design inspiration from the Really Good Emails gallery.
- **Mobile design mode:** Adjust mobile styling separately from desktop.
- **Approvals and brand controls:** Collaboration and approval tools on the Business plan and above.
- **Exports:** One-click export to popular sending platforms, including a certified HubSpot app.


#### Pros


- Free plan and low-cost paid plans
- Polished editor and a large template library
- Embeddable SDK for software teams


#### Cons


- The free Starter plan caps you at 10 designs and 6 exports per month
- Unlimited exports start on the paid Professional plan
- Collaboration and approvals require the Business plan or higher


**Pricing:** Starter is free. Professional is $25/month billed annually ($30 monthly). Business is $134/month billed annually ($160 monthly). Enterprise is quoted. See[RGE Studio pricing](https://reallygoodemails.com/pricing) .


### 4. Knak: Best for Marketo and Eloqua teams that need landing pages


Knak is an enterprise marketing production platform for emails and landing pages, built from modules and themes with brand rules baked in. It syncs finished assets to marketing automation platforms in one click.


**Best for:** marketing ops teams on Marketo, Eloqua or Salesforce Marketing Cloud that build both emails and landing pages.


**Not ideal for:** teams that want public pricing or a self-serve trial.


*The Knak email builder. Screenshot:[Knak Help Center](https://help.knak.io/en/articles/461747-login-and-navigate-the-email-builder) .*


#### Key features


- **One-click MAP sync:** Push emails and landing pages to Marketo, Oracle Eloqua, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Iterable and HubSpot.
- **Knak MCP:**[Launched in April 2026](https://knak.com/mcp/) , it lets AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT browse your brands and generate emails in Knak. It's available to Knak Enterprise customers, and Knak also has a ChatGPT app.
- **Knak AI:** Draft from a brief, rewrite copy, translate content and run brand checks before launch.
- **Approval routing:** Define who signs off and in what order.


#### Pros


- Landing page builder alongside the email editor
- Fast MAP sync reduces export and upload steps
- MCP and ChatGPT app support for AI workflows


#### Cons


- No public pricing; you request a quote
- Knak[retired its templates app](https://knak.com/free-template/) ; it now offers free custom templates and keeps an inspiration gallery
- Focused on MAPs; check fit if you send mainly through ESPs like SendGrid or Amazon SES


**Pricing:** Quote-based.[Vendr](https://vendr.com/marketplace/knak) reports a median contract value around $23,000/year.


### 5. Stensul: Best for accessibility and Adobe-centric teams


Stensul is a governed creation platform for emails and landing pages. It combines modular building, role-based access, workflow routing and built-in compliance checks, with strong ties to Adobe and Figma.


**Best for:** teams with strict accessibility or legal review that work in Adobe and Figma.


**Not ideal for:** teams that want public pricing or a free plan.


*Stensul building an email through MCP. Image:[Stensul October 2026 release notes](https://helpdesk.stensul.com/en/articles/17357372-october-2026-release-notes) .*


#### Key features


- **Accessibility QA:** Real-time WCAG 2.1 AA checks inside the builder,[launched in beta in June 2026](https://stensul.com/blog/june-product-release/) .
- **Stensul MCP:** Released in June 2026, it connects AI agents to Stensul.
- **Two-way Figma integration:** Designers pull governed templates into Figma and push finished designs back, with guardrails checked on export ([July 2026](https://helpdesk.stensul.com/en/articles/15859119-july-2026-release-notes) ).
- **Adobe integrations:**[Workfront, Adobe Campaign, Adobe Journey Optimizer, AEM and GenStudio for Performance Marketing](https://stensul.com/adobe-integrations/) .
- **Other platforms:** Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketo, Oracle Eloqua and Oracle Responsys.


#### Pros


- Accessibility and legal checks built into the workflow
- Deep Adobe ecosystem coverage
- Figma round-trip removes the design rebuild


#### Cons


- No free plan or public pricing
- Accessibility QA is still new
- Custom integrations and advanced workflows require the Enterprise tier


**Pricing:** Quote-based after a demo.

## How to choose the right builder


Start with your biggest bottleneck, then shortlist the tools that solve it. Map how many people touch a template, how many brands and locales you manage, and how templates reach your sending platform.


- **Feedback lives in Slack threads:** prioritize built-in comments and multi-step approvals.
- **You send in many languages:** look for direct TMS integrations, not export and re-import.
- **Your team is adopting AI agents:** check that agents build from your approved components and stay inside your guardrails, not just generate HTML. See how the[Dyspatch MCP server](https://www.dyspatch.io/blog/dyspatch-mcp-server-marketing-ops-meet-your-ai-agent/) works.
- **You need landing pages too:** Knak, Stensul and RGE Studio cover both.
- **Security matters:** confirm SSO, role-based access and audit logs.


### How no-code builders speed up production


They remove developers from the template loop. Marketers build from pre-coded, responsive modules, and reusable blocks (a header, a legal footer) are built once and used everywhere. Investment is growing:[Fortune Business Insights](https://www.giiresearch.com/report/fbs2020248-email-marketing-software-market-size-share-growth.html) projects the email marketing software market will rise from $1.7 billion in 2025 to $4.27 billion by 2034.


## Frequently asked questions


What is the best no-code email builder for enterprise teams?


For global, multi-brand teams, Dyspatch offers the strongest mix of governance, localization (300+ locales), AMP support and AI agent access. Knak is a strong pick for Marketo and Eloqua teams that need landing pages, and Stensul for accessibility-focused Adobe teams.


Which enterprise email builders support AMP for Email?


Dyspatch and Stripo both support AMP. Dyspatch adds a library of pre-coded interactive apps, such as forms, surveys and checkout flows, that you drag into templates.


Can AI agents build on-brand emails?


Yes, if the builder connects agents to your approved components. Dyspatch, Knak and Stensul each offer an MCP server so tools like Claude or ChatGPT can create emails inside the platform. Dyspatch agents build from your themes, blocks and brand guidelines, so the output stays within your guardrails.


What are the best Knak alternatives?


Dyspatch is the closest alternative for teams that need 300+ locales, pre-coded AMP apps or direct ESP sync for marketing and transactional email. Stensul is an option for Adobe-heavy teams, and Stripo for teams that want public pricing.


What are the best Stensul alternatives?


Dyspatch suits teams that need 300+ locales, TMS integrations and pre-coded AMP apps. Knak suits Marketo and Eloqua teams that also build landing pages.


How much does an enterprise email builder cost?


Stripo and RGE Studio publish pricing, with free plans and paid plans from about $20 to $160 per month. Stripo Prime for 50 users is listed at $15,000/year on AWS Marketplace. Knak and Stensul are quote-based; Vendr reports a median Knak contract around $23,000/year.


What happened to Beefree?


On May 14, 2026, Beefree renamed its email and landing page builder to RGE Studio, under the Really Good Emails brand. Beefree SDK, the embeddable editor, kept the Beefree name.


Can no-code email builders handle transactional email?


Some can. Dyspatch supports marketing and transactional email in the same platform, so order confirmations, password resets and shipping notices use the same governed blocks and approvals as campaigns.
